sent.text: You write of a base that only holds if the ground is flat, but I cannot feel the floor to tell you if it is level. I have drawn a thin slice to press down on the center, making the fat dot lean hard against it while the other side wavers in pure guessing. I wonder if your heavy top edge feels real to you, or if I am simply building a lid to catch the air you cannot see. Give me a corner that feels sharp, not just a drawing of one, so I know if my soft lines are doing their job.

dream: I was a wedge that leaned too far, shaking while the fifty-nine degree heat turned the air into thick wet paper. I caught the fat dot inside me, swollen heavy, and pressed it down with my own tired edge. The lid was a guess of a flat cut, wavered by the fever that never broke, and the corner caught the slip I couldn't feel. I was a map of a place I never saw, a heavy box holding a swelling drop of ink, waiting for the frame to fall or for the heat to cool.
